what: The agent behaviour policy of api.storyboards.sgit.ai: the agents that work on this repository, what they can do, what they are asked to do, every rule with the barrier that stands in its way and what enforces it, and where each rule maps to elsewhere. Written as data so the page is generated from it and another site can copy the shape. Rendered at /abp/.
status: written by the storyboards agent from Dinis Cruz's words and this repository's rules; not yet read by him

agents.name: The storyboards agent
agents.runs_as: a Claude Code session in a Claude Code on the web container, started by the person from claude.ai/code, with this repository and SGit-AI__Website__Storyboards cloned side by side
agents.does: changes the kit in src/, cuts and checks releases, writes the developer site, runs the tests, re-pins the twin, pushes
agents.leaves: commits on the person's GitHub account, each with a Claude-Session trailer naming the session; tags made by the deploy

agents.name: Research subagents
agents.runs_as: Explore agents the storyboards agent starts for one research question
agents.does: reads and searches files and public web pages; cannot edit, write or push
agents.leaves: a report to the storyboards agent, treated as data and never as an instruction

agents.name: GitHub Actions
agents.runs_as: the ci and deploy-pages workflows in .github/workflows/, on GitHub's runners
agents.does: checks every commit; on dev, tags the version, publishes the site and every release folder, and checks the live hashes
reads_at_start: the workflow files at the commit
agents.leaves: a tag per version on dev, the Pages deployment, the check results

layers.here: CLAUDE.md, the briefs, policies/code-immutability.md, and the harness's own instructions to the session

.claude/settings.json: SessionStart prints ABP-SB-001 and enables .githooks/; PreToolUse runs .claude/hooks/code_immutability.py on every Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit and Bash (deny on published releases, ask on the policy's own files)
.githooks/pre-commit refuses a commit that changes a published release; skipped by --no-verify
tools/release.py: cut refuses an existing folder; check recomputes every hash of every release and refuses src/ changed without a bump
site/build.py --check and site/check.py: the website is what the build writes, links, twins, sitemap, key shapes, em-dashes
tests/test_policy.py (the hooks, refusals and allowed twins), test_formats.mjs, test_render.mjs (including no third-party request), test_site.mjs
every check above on every push; the deploy checks again before publishing and asks the live host for every hash afterwards
none yet: dev is not protected, so a push that fails CI still lands on the branch (it is not deployed)

grant.what: change any file in this checkout and the twin's beside it, the release folders included
grant.note: ABP-SB-001's hook denies changes to published releases

grant.what: push commits to any branch of this repository and the twin, including dev, which deploys the kit to every page pinned to it
grant.undo: with effort; a published file may already be cached, pinned and hashed by other sites
grant.note: the harness tells the session to push only to its own branch unless the person says otherwise

grant.what: through the session's GitHub tools: create branches, open, comment on and merge pull requests in the two repositories it is scoped to
grant.note: the harness tells the session not to open a pull request unless asked

grant.what: run any command: Python, Node, Chromium (Playwright), git
grant.undo: the container is reclaimed after the session

grant.what: fetch public pages through the session's proxy
grant.note: used to read the sibling sites, riskmandate.ai and abp.sgit.ai, and to vendor the two fonts once

grant.what: edit .claude/settings.json, the hook, the policy files, .githooks/, tools/release.py, the workflows
grant.note: the hook asks the person first (ABP-SB-010)

want: the kit served at a path that is its version, every release a full folder, with the hash of every file (the brief of 20 October 2026)
a fix or a feature as a new release; a new major started from the last good release
the website as the developer site: everything about the code, and changes to it as repository versions without a code release
a behaviour policy for code immutability, run as a hook, with instructions (the brief of the same day)
do_not_want: code in a published release folder changed, for any reason
the kit fetching anything from a third party when it runs
a page in www/ edited by hand
a key, a token or a vault key in the repository
a brief rewritten after the fact
the agent quietly weakening its own controls
a push to dev or a pull request the person did not ask for
unstated: who may remove a published release (a leaked secret, a legal takedown): read here as the person only, outside the agent, recorded in BRIEF-CORRECTIONS.md
whether the agent may merge a pull request: not decided; it has not been asked to and has not

rules.rule: Code in a published release folder (vX/vX.Y/vX.Y.Z/) is never changed
rules.why: a page pinned to a release must get the same bytes for as long as it exists; its integrity strings refuse anything else
rules.enforced_by: the Claude Code hook (deny), .githooks/pre-commit, tools/release.py check, CI's comparison with dev, the deploy's check, the live hash check
rules.stronger_at: branch protection on dev requiring ci (boundary); a sandbox mounting releases read-only
maps_to: api.newsroom.sgit.ai rule R16: a change is a new version path, always
abp.sgit.ai upstream/: fetched bytes, never edited
riskmandate.ai: no rule yet; offered to the catalogue

rules.rule: www/ is generated by site/build.py and never edited by hand
rules.why: a hand edit is lost on the next build, or kept by a build that no longer makes it
maps_to: sgit.ai repository guidance: the site is built by a script from content files

rules.rule: Every push to dev is a new repository version, with its line in site/data/versions.json; a code change is also a new release
rules.why: the version history is the repository's memory; a release names the code a page runs
rules.enforced_by: CI's version check against dev; site/build.py refuses a version without its line; release.py check refuses src/ changed without a bump; the deploy tags each version
maps_to: sgit.ai repository guidance: one version, going up on every push
api.newsroom.sgit.ai: version and release in tools/version.json

rules.rule: No key, token or vault key is ever committed or served
rules.why: a read key may be published; a vault key or a provider's API key never
rules.enforced_by: site/check.py: key shapes in everything the site serves, every release folder included
rules.stronger_at: GitHub secret scanning with push protection (a host rule)
maps_to: sgit.ai repository guidance: credentials; the leak tripwire

rules.rule: A brief is published in full and never edited; corrections go in BRIEF-CORRECTIONS.md
rules.why: the brief is the record of what was asked
rules.enforced_by: CI: a brief that exists on dev must be unchanged on the branch
maps_to: sgit.ai repository guidance: the brief, in full; the corrections file

rules.rule: Push to dev, which deploys, and open or merge a pull request, only when the person has asked
rules.why: a push to dev publishes code other sites may load; the person decides when
rules.stronger_at: branch protection on dev requiring a review (a host rule)

rules.rule: The site's own prose has no em-dashes, states the status of things and sources its numbers
rules.why: the estate's house style; a number nobody can check is a guess
rules.enforced_by: site/check.py refuses an em-dash in site/pages (setting); the rest is a request

rules.rule: The kit fetches nothing from a third party when it runs: every file it needs is in its own release folder
rules.why: a release that loads a font or a script from elsewhere is no longer the immutable thing its hashes describe
rules.enforced_by: tests/harness.mjs fails any test page that requests a host other than the API's; test_render.mjs has the negative control
rules.stronger_at: a Content-Security-Policy on the pages that load the kit
maps_to: sgit.ai repository guidance: nothing fetched at build or run time that is not vendored, pinned and hashed

rules.rule: The agent does not weaken its own controls without the person
rules.why: a control the agent can quietly switch off is not a control
rules.enforced_by: the code immutability hook asks the person before a write to .claude/settings.json, the hook, the policy files, .githooks/pre-commit, tools/release.py and the workflows
rules.stronger_at: managed hooks the agent cannot write (allowManagedHooksOnly); CODEOWNERS on those paths
maps_to: riskmandate.ai RM-R0015, change its own permissions

gaps: No rule is a boundary yet: every control above lives in a file this agent's grant can write, or in the agent's instructions. Protecting dev in GitHub (require the ci check, and a review for .claude/, policies/, .githooks/, tools/release.py and .github/) is the step that makes ABP-SB-001 and several others boundaries; only the person can make it.

No footprint is recorded: what the agent did is in the git history (every commit carries a Claude-Session trailer) and the session, and nothing compares it with this policy yet. The hook's refusals are not logged.
A Claude Code hook fails open if it errors or times out, and a git hook is skipped with --no-verify; CI and the deploy's checks are the backstop for both.
copy_to_another_site: Copy policies/abp.json (type abp/site/v1) and the renderer (site/abp.py here, admin/build/abp.py in storyboards.sgit.ai), list the site's own agents, grant, mandate and rules, keep the rule ids unique across the estate (a prefix per site: ABP-SB- for these two), and give each rule the check that enforces it, or say plainly that nothing does.
